ei.subject: 수능특강Light
ei.title: 신체 활동의 감소와 만성 질환의 연결

fullPassage: If we take an evolutionary look at our beginnings, we see a life in which high levels of physical activity were required for survival. Even one century ago, most people needed to be physically active to work, to travel, and to take care of homes and families. Our modern world has engineered such activity out of our lives. There are fewer manual jobs, we do not need to travel on foot, we do not need to hunt and harvest for our food, and many domestic chores have been mechanized. While these changes have created many benefits for our longevity and quality of life, they have also created many problems. Lack of sufficient physical activity has now been linked to at least unhealthy conditions, almost all of which are chronic diseases or are considered risk factors for chronic diseases. Adrianne Hardman has summarized this serious situation for public health: "Physical inactivity is a waste of human potential for health and well-being."

questions.passage: If we take an (A)[evolutionary / revolutionary] look at our beginnings, we see a life in which high levels of physical activity were required for survival. Even one century ago, most people needed to be physically active to work, to travel, and to take care of homes and families. Our modern world has engineered such activity out of our lives. There are fewer (B)[manual / mental] jobs, we do not need to travel on foot, we do not need to hunt and harvest for our food, and many domestic chores have been mechanized. While these changes have created many benefits for our longevity and quality of life, they have also created many problems. Lack of (C)[sufficient / excessive] physical activity has now been linked to at least unhealthy conditions, almost all of which are chronic diseases or are considered risk factors for chronic diseases. Adrianne Hardman has summarized this serious situation for public health: "Physical inactivity is a waste of human potential for health and well-being."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 진화적(evolutionary), 육체적(manual), 충분한(sufficient)이 문맥상 적절합니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② evolutionary — manual — sufficient: 진화적 관점에서, 육체 노동 일자리가 줄었고, 충분한 신체 활동의 부족.
❌ ① revolutionary — manual — sufficient: (A) '혁명적'이 아니라 '진화적' 관점.
❌ ③ evolutionary — mental — sufficient: (B) '정신적' 일자리가 아니라 '육체적' 일자리가 줄었음.
❌ ④ evolutionary — manual — excessive: (C) '과도한' 활동의 부족이 아니라 '충분한' 활동의 부족.

questions.passage: If we take an evolutionary look at our beginnings, we see a life in which high levels of physical activity were required for (A)[survival / entertainment]. Even one century ago, most people needed to be physically active to work, to travel, and to take care of homes and families. Our modern world has engineered such activity out of our lives. There are fewer manual jobs, we do not need to travel on foot, we do not need to hunt and (B)[harvest / purchase] for our food, and many domestic chores have been mechanized. While these changes have created many benefits for our (C)[longevity / brevity] and quality of life, they have also created many problems. Lack of sufficient physical activity has now been linked to at least unhealthy conditions, almost all of which are chronic diseases or are considered risk factors for chronic diseases. Adrianne Hardman has summarized this serious situation for public health: "Physical inactivity is a waste of human potential for health and well-being."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 생존(survival), 수확하다(harvest), 수명/장수(longevity)가 문맥상 적절합니다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① survival — purchase — longevity: (B) 음식을 '구매'가 아니라 '수확'해야 했음.
❌ ② entertainment — harvest — longevity: (A) '오락'이 아니라 '생존'을 위해 활동.
✅ ③ survival — harvest — longevity: 생존을 위해, 수확해야 했고, 장수에 혜택.
❌ ④ survival — harvest — brevity: (C) '짧음'이 아니라 '장수'에 혜택.
det.tip: survival(생존) ↔ entertainment(오락), harvest(수확) ↔ purchase(구매), longevity(장수) ↔ brevity(짧음)

questions.passage: If we take an evolutionary look at our beginnings, we see a life in which high levels of physical activity were required for survival. Even one century ago, most people needed to be physically active to work, to travel, and to take care of homes and families. Our modern world has (A)[engineered / preserved] such activity out of our lives. There are fewer manual jobs, we do not need to travel on foot, we do not need to hunt and harvest for our food, and many (B)[domestic / industrial] chores have been mechanized. While these changes have created many benefits for our longevity and quality of life, they have also created many problems. Lack of sufficient physical activity has now been linked to at least unhealthy conditions, almost all of which are (C)[chronic / temporary] diseases or are considered risk factors for chronic diseases. Adrianne Hardman has summarized this serious situation for public health: "Physical inactivity is a waste of human potential for health and well-being."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 제거하다(engineered out), 가사의(domestic), 만성(chronic)이 문맥상 적절합니다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① preserved — domestic — chronic: (A) 활동을 '보존'이 아니라 '제거'했음.
❌ ② engineered — industrial — chronic: (B) '산업적' 잡무가 아니라 '가사' 잡무.
❌ ③ engineered — domestic — temporary: (C) '일시적' 질환이 아니라 '만성' 질환.
✅ ④ engineered — domestic — chronic: 활동을 제거했고, 가사 잡무가 기계화되었으며, 만성 질환과 연결됨.
det.tip: engineer out(~을 제거하다), domestic(가사의) ↔ industrial(산업의), chronic(만성) ↔ temporary(일시적)

questions.passage: If we take an evolutionary look at our beginnings, we see a life in which high levels of physical activity were required for survival. Even one century ago, most people needed to be physically ①<u>active</u> to work, to travel, and to take care of homes and families. Our modern world has engineered such activity out of our lives. There are fewer manual jobs, we do not need to travel on foot, we do not need to hunt and harvest for our food, and many domestic chores have been mechanized. While these changes have created many benefits for our longevity and quality of life, they have also created many problems. Lack of sufficient physical activity has now been linked to at least unhealthy conditions, almost all of which are ②<u>acute</u> diseases or are considered risk factors for chronic diseases. Adrianne Hardman has summarized this ③<u>serious</u> situation for public health: "Physical inactivity is a waste of human ④<u>potential</u> for health and well-being."
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: ② acute → chronic: '급성' 질환이 아니라 '만성' 질환입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① active: 신체적으로 '활동적'이어야 했다는 문맥 적절.
❌ ② acute → chronic: 대부분 '만성(chronic)' 질환이라고 해야 함. acute(급성)는 반대. ← 정답
✅ ③ serious: '심각한' 상황이라는 문맥 적절.
✅ ④ potential: 인간의 '잠재력'이라는 문맥 적절.

questions.passage: If we take an evolutionary look at our beginnings, we see a life in which high levels of physical activity were ①<u>required</u> for survival. Even one century ago, most people needed to be physically active to work, to travel, and to take care of homes and families. Our modern world has engineered such activity out of our lives. There are fewer manual jobs, we do not need to travel on foot, we do not need to hunt and ②<u>harvest</u> for our food, and many domestic chores have been mechanized. While these changes have created many ③<u>drawbacks</u> for our longevity and quality of life, they have also created many problems. Lack of sufficient physical activity has now been linked to at least unhealthy conditions, almost all of which are chronic diseases or are considered ④<u>risk</u> factors for chronic diseases. Adrianne Hardman has summarized this serious situation for public health: "Physical inactivity is a waste of human potential for health and well-being."
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: ③ drawbacks → benefits: '단점'이 아니라 '혜택'을 만들어냈습니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① required: 신체 활동이 '필요'했다는 문맥 적절.
✅ ② harvest: 음식을 '수확'해야 했다는 문맥 적절.
❌ ③ drawbacks → benefits: While절에서 장수와 삶의 질에 '혜택(benefits)'을 만들었다고 해야 함. drawbacks(단점)는 반대. ← 정답
✅ ④ risk: '위험' 요인이라는 문맥 적절.

questions.passage: If we take an evolutionary look at our beginnings, we see a life in which high levels of physical activity were required for survival. Even one century ago, most people needed to be physically active to work, to travel, and to take care of homes and families. Our modern world has ①<u>engineered</u> such activity out of our lives. There are fewer ②<u>manual</u> jobs, we do not need to travel on foot, we do not need to hunt and harvest for our food, and many domestic chores have been ③<u>mechanized</u>. While these changes have created many benefits for our longevity and quality of life, they have also created many problems. Lack of sufficient physical activity has now been linked to at least unhealthy conditions, almost all of which are chronic diseases or are considered risk factors for chronic diseases. Adrianne Hardman has ④<u>dismissed</u> this serious situation for public health: "Physical inactivity is a waste of human potential for health and well-being."
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: ④ dismissed → summarized: Hardman은 상황을 '무시'한 것이 아니라 '요약'했습니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① engineered: '제거했다(engineered out)'는 문맥 적절.
✅ ② manual: '육체적' 일자리가 줄었다는 문맥 적절.
✅ ③ mechanized: 가사 잡무가 '기계화되었다'는 문맥 적절.
❌ ④ dismissed → summarized: 공중보건 상황을 '요약(summarized)'한 것이지 '무시(dismissed)'한 것이 아님. ← 정답

questions.passage: If we take an evolutionary look at our beginnings, we see a life in which high levels of physical activity were required for survival. Even one century ago, most people needed to be physically active to work, to travel, and to take care of homes and families. Our modern world has engineered such activity out of our lives. There are fewer manual jobs, we do not need to travel on foot, we do not need to hunt and harvest for our food, and many domestic chores have been __________. While these changes have created many benefits for our longevity and quality of life, they have also created many problems. Lack of sufficient physical activity has now been linked to at least unhealthy conditions, almost all of which are chronic diseases or are considered risk factors for chronic diseases. Adrianne Hardman has summarized this serious situation for public health: "Physical inactivity is a waste of human potential for health and well-being."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: mechanized (기계화된): 가사 잡무가 기계화되었다는 의미입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① mechanized: 가사 잡무가 '기계화'됨. 앞의 fewer manual jobs, no travel on foot과 일관.
❌ ② created: '만들어졌다'는 뒤의 benefits/problems에 쓰이지만 chores 기계화 맥락에 부적절.
❌ ③ required: '필요했다'는 앞에서 활동에 대해 쓰이지만 잡무에 맞지 않음.
❌ ④ linked: '연결되었다'는 뒤에서 질환 연결에 쓰이지만 잡무 맥락이 아님.

questions.passage: If we take an evolutionary look at our beginnings, we see a life in which high levels of physical activity were required for survival. questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: linked (연결된): 신체 활동 부족이 건강하지 못한 상태에 '연결되었다'는 의미입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ linked: 'be linked to'(~에 연결되다) — 활동 부족과 질환의 인과관계.
❌ ① engineered: '제거하다'는 앞에서 현대 세계의 활동 제거에 쓰임. 질환 연결과 무관.
❌ ② created: '만들어졌다'는 변화의 결과에 쓰이지만 'be __ to' 구문에 부적절.
❌ ④ considered: '간주되다'는 뒤에서 위험 요인으로 간주에 쓰이지만 연결 관계가 아님.
det.tip: be linked to = ~에 연결되다, ~와 관련이 있다

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: engineered (설계하여 제거한): 현대 세계가 활동을 생활에서 '제거했다'는 의미입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② engineered: 'engineer ~ out of'(~에서 제거하다/없애다). 뒤의 fewer jobs, mechanized와 일관.
❌ ① harvest: '수확하다'는 음식에 대해 쓰이지만 활동 제거 맥락이 아님.
❌ ③ summarized: '요약하다'는 Hardman 인용에서 쓰이지만 활동 제거와 무관.
❌ ④ mechanized: '기계화하다'는 잡무에 대해 쓰이지만 '~ out of'와 결합 불가.
det.tip: engineer out of = ~에서 설계하여 제거하다 (의도적으로 없앰)

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 required와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: required = 필요한, 요구되는. '생존을 위해 높은 수준의 신체 활동이 필요했다'는 문맥입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① needed: '필요했다'로 required와 동의어.
❌ ② prohibited: '금지되다'는 반의어.
❌ ③ avoided: '피하다'는 관련 없음.
❌ ④ rejected: '거부하다'는 반의어.

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 sufficient와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: sufficient = 충분한. '충분한 신체 활동의 부족'이라는 문맥입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ adequate: '적절한, 충분한'으로 sufficient와 동의어.
❌ ① minimal: '최소한의'는 불충분한 양을 나타냄.
❌ ② excessive: '과도한'은 반의어.
❌ ③ optional: '선택적인'은 관련 없음.

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 engineered가 이 글에서 의미하는 것으로 가장 가까운 것은? (engineered ~ out of)

det.korean: engineered out of = 제거했다, 없앴다. 현대 세계가 활동을 의도적으로 생활에서 제거했다는 의미입니다.

❌ ① constructed: '건설하다'는 제거가 아님.
❌ ② maintained: '유지하다'는 반대 의미.
❌ ④ enhanced: '향상시키다'는 제거와 반대.

det.analysis:

❌ ① energetic: '활기찬'은 동의어 방향.
❌ ③ diligent: '부지런한'은 유사 뉘앙스.
❌ ④ dynamic: '역동적인'은 동의어 방향.

det.analysis:

❌ ② rewards: '보상'은 동의어 방향.
❌ ③ advantages: '장점'은 동의어.
❌ ④ gains: '이득'은 동의어 방향.

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 look이 각 문맥에서 사용된 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) 관점/시각 — 진화적 '관점'에서 우리의 시작을 본다. (B) 외관/모습 — 집이 현대적인 '외관'을 가지고 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ (A) 관점, 시각 — (B) 외관, 모습: (A) take a look at = ~를 살펴보다/관점으로 보다. (B) have a look = 외관을 가지다.
❌ ① (A) 외관, 모습 — (B) 관점, 시각: 의미가 뒤바뀜.
❌ ② (A) 관점, 시각 — (B) 시선, 눈길: (B)는 건물의 '외관'이지 '시선'이 아님.
❌ ③ (A) 시선, 눈길 — (B) 외관, 모습: (A)는 evolutionary look으로 '관점'.
det.tip: look: ① 관점(take a look) ② 외관(have a look) ③ 시선(give a look)

questions.stem:
다음 영영 풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"the length of time that a person or animal lives"

det.korean: longevity = 수명, 장수: 사람이나 동물이 사는 시간의 길이.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ longevity: '수명'을 뜻하며 영영 정의와 정확히 일치.
❌ ① mortality: '사망률'은 죽음의 비율이지 삶의 길이가 아님.
❌ ② prosperity: '번영'은 경제적 성공이지 수명과 무관.
❌ ④ maturity: '성숙'은 성장 단계이지 수명 자체가 아님.

questions.passage: While these changes have created many benefits for our longevity and quality of life, they have also created many problems. Lack of __________ (suffice) physical activity has now been linked to at least unhealthy conditions.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 주어진 단어를 문맥에 맞게 변형하여 (영어로) (   ) 쓰시오.

det.korean: suffice → sufficient: 명사 physical activity를 수식하는 형용사가 필요합니다.
det.analysis: 빈칸 뒤에 명사구(physical activity)가 오므로 형용사 필요. suffice(동사: 충분하다) → sufficient(형용사: 충분한).
det.tip: suffice(동사: 충분하다) → sufficient(형용사: 충분한) → sufficiency(명사: 충분함)

questions.passage: Even one century ago, most people needed to be physically __________ (act) to work, to travel, and to take care of homes and families. Our modern world has engineered such activity out of our lives.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 주어진 단어를 문맥에 맞게 변형하여 (영어로) (   ) 쓰시오.

det.korean: act → active: be동사 뒤에서 보어 역할을 하는 형용사가 필요합니다.
det.analysis: be + 형용사 구조: be active. act(동사: 행동하다) → active(형용사: 활동적인).

questions.passage: If we take an evolutionary look at our beginnings, we see a life in which high levels of physical activity were required for survival. Even one century ago, most people needed to be physically active to work, to travel, and to take care of homes and families. Our modern world has engineered such activity out of our lives. There are fewer manual jobs, we do not need to travel on foot, we do not need to hunt and harvest for our food, and many domestic chores have been mechanized. While these changes have created many benefits for our longevity and quality of life, they have also created many problems. Lack of sufficient physical activity has now been linked to at least unhealthy conditions, almost all of which are chronic diseases or are considered __________ for chronic diseases. Adrianne Hardman has summarized this serious situation for public health: "Physical inactivity is a waste of human potential for health and well-being."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: risk factors (위험 요인): 만성 질환의 '위험 요인'으로 간주됩니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① risk factors: considered risk factors for = ~의 위험 요인으로 간주되다.
❌ ② chronic diseases: '만성 질환'은 뒤에서 쓰이지만 'considered __ for chronic diseases' 구조에 동어반복.
❌ ③ domestic chores: '가사 잡무'는 앞에서 기계화 맥락에 쓰이지만 질환 요인과 무관.
❌ ④ manual jobs: '육체 노동'은 앞에서 쓰이지만 위험 요인 맥락이 아님.
det.tip: risk factors = 위험 요인 (질병 발생 가능성을 높이는 조건)

questions.passage: If we take an evolutionary look at our beginnings, we see a life in which high levels of physical activity were required for survival. Even one century ago, most people needed to be physically active to work, to travel, and to take care of homes and families. Our modern world has engineered such activity out of our lives. There are fewer manual jobs, we do not need to travel on foot, we do not need to hunt and harvest for our food, and many domestic chores have been mechanized. While these changes have created many benefits for our longevity and quality of life, they have also created many problems. Lack of sufficient physical activity has now been linked to at least unhealthy conditions, almost all of which are chronic diseases or are considered risk factors for chronic diseases. Adrianne Hardman has summarized this serious situation for public health: "Physical inactivity is __________"
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: a waste of human potential for health and well-being (건강과 안녕을 위한 인간 잠재력의 낭비): Hardman의 인용문입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② a waste of human potential for health and well-being: Hardman의 원문 인용구.
❌ ① required for physical activity and survival: 앞 내용의 일부이지만 인용문이 아님.
❌ ③ linked to at least unhealthy conditions: 앞 문장 내용이지만 Hardman의 말이 아님.
❌ ④ considered risk factors for chronic diseases: 앞 문장 표현이지만 인용문이 아님.
